title: Broker’s Call: Endurance Tech (Buy) - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Endurance Technologies continues to strengthen its manufacturing capabilities through targeted capacity additions. In braking systems, the company is adding about 0.9 million ABS capacity to its existing 0.64 million units, with SOP expected by September/October 2026, while new dual-channel ABS programmes for Bajaj Auto are scheduled to commence in Q1/Q3FY27. The new Chennai disc brake facility, with a capacity of about 3 million assemblies, is expected to commence supplies to Royal Enfield in September 2026, with other OEMs following in Q3FY27.

In suspension, the management targets monthly inverted front fork capacity of about one lakh units by FY27, while new programmes with Bajaj Auto, Hero MotoCorp and Suzuki are expected to ramp up from Q3FY27. The company is also scaling its four-wheeler aluminium casting business, with cumulative bookings of about ₹513 crore per annum at Shendra.

The company is steadily strengthening its presence across the EV value chain through battery packs, BMS, motor controllers, DC-DC converters and aluminium castings. The battery pack plant near Pune commenced SOP for Hero MotoCorp in June and is expected to reach peak volumes by Q3FY27, with the company also investing ₹62 crore to enter four-wheeler battery packs, with SOP targeted for Q4FY27.

We maintain our Buy rating on Endurance Technologies, led by strong order visibility, EV traction and upcoming capacities supporting medium-term growth momentum.
